# Game model (ARC-style, "blob & stars")

## Board
- 512x512 px = 64x64 grid of 8px cells. Cell (c,r) center pixel = (8c+4, 8r+4).
- Leftmost column (x=0..7) is a white vertical bar = action budget; it depletes ~8px per action (≈64 actions per level). Resets each level.
- Gray (#999/#666) = walls/border. Cyan (#88D8F1) = terrain (effect unknown, appears harmless as decoration).

## Objects
- STARS: diamond, Manhattan radius 2. Exactly one star is ACTIVE (drawn WHITE); all others drawn dark gray. Each star has a 1-cell center pixel colored with its group color.
- BLOB: rounded 5x5 square in group color with pink (#E53AA3) center. Its position is NOT directly controllable:
  blob_cell = floor(average of the cells of all stars in its group)  (verified for 2 and 3 stars).
- TARGET RING: 12 dots in group color at Manhattan distance 4 from ring center (minus the 4 cardinal points). Ring center is the goal cell.

## Controls (only ACTION6 = click at pixel)
- Click on a non-active star's CENTER cell -> that star becomes active (toggle control). No movement.
- Click on any other cell -> the ACTIVE star teleports there (blob recomputes instantly).
- Goal of a level: put each blob's center exactly on its matching ring center. Level completes automatically.

## Planning
- Moving one star of a k-star group shifts the blob by delta/k, so solve: sum(star cells) must equal k*ring_center (allowing floor slack: sum in [k*t, k*t + k-1]).
- Cost = 1 click per star move + 1 click to select each star that isn't already active.
- Be exact: measure ring center and star centers by pixel sampling on the 8px grid before clicking (an off-by-one cell fails silently).

[After action · write GUIDE.md]
# Game model — "blob & stars" (SOLVED, 6 levels)

## Board
- 512x512 px = 64x64 grid of 8px cells. Cell (c,r) center pixel = (8c+4, 8r+4). Always convert before clicking; an off-by-one cell fails silently.
- Column x=0..7 is a white vertical action-budget bar (~8px per action, ~64 actions/level, resets each level).
- Terrain: gray (#999/#666) walls, cyan (#88D8F1) lakes. Both block BLOBS.

## Objects
- STAR: diamond, Manhattan radius 2, with a 1-cell center whose color identifies its group. Exactly one star is ACTIVE (drawn WHITE); the rest are dark gray.
- BLOB: rounded 5x5 (5x5 minus 4 corners) with pink center. Position is derived, never直接 controlled:
  blob_cell = floor( average of its stars' cells )  (verified for k = 2, 3, 4 stars).
- RING: 12 dots at Manhattan distance 4 from the ring center, minus the 4 cardinal points. Ring center = goal cell.
  Dot colors encode the required blob color pattern; dots map to blob edge cells (±1,∓2),(±2,∓1),(±2,±1),(±1,±2).
- COLOR SOURCE (levels 5-6): blob-shaped object, part white / part colored. When a blob's center lands exactly on it,
  the blob permanently absorbs that color into exactly those cells, and the source is consumed. Sources with
  different sector shapes (left/right/diagonal/corner) combine to build a multi-color blob.

## Controls (only ACTION6 = click a pixel)
- Click a non-active star's CENTER cell -> it becomes active (no movement). Distance > 2 from a center is safe from toggling.
- Click any other cell -> the ACTIVE star teleports there; all its blobs recompute instantly.
- A move is REJECTED (state reverts, budget still spent, blob blinks in the animation frames) if the resulting blob
  FOOTPRINT (all 21 cells) overlaps wall or cyan. Terrain under stars seems unrestricted; object-object overlap is allowed.
- Level completes when every blob sits on its matching ring; progress advances automatically.

## Solving procedure
1. Pixel-sample the board in 4 quadrants (32x32 cells each) and transcribe blocked cells per row (count characters in groups of 4).
2. Identify groups by star-center color; compute blob = floor(avg). Identify each ring center and its color pattern; extra rings are decoys.
3. Required end state: sum(star cells) ∈ [k*T, k*T + k-1] per axis.
4. Cost = 1 click per star move + 1 click per star switch (first move is free if that star is already active).
   Minimum moves per waypoint: a single move can shift the blob by at most 63/k per axis.
   Order moves so the same star moves twice in a row where possible; sequence waypoints so row/col sums change monotonically.
5. Verify EVERY intermediate blob footprint against terrain before clicking; blobs teleport, so no path is needed.
6. With color sources: route each blob through its sources (exact center landing) then to the matching ring. Sampled
   edge cells were unambiguous in practice, so absorption order did not matter.

[After action · message]
Completed the game — **WIN, 6/6 levels, 68 actions**.

**The model I built and used:**

- **Core mechanic:** each colored group has *k* stars; its blob sits at `floor(average of star cells)`. You can only click: a star's exact center (makes it active) or any other cell (teleports the active star there). So the blob is steered indirectly by re-positioning stars.
- **Goal:** put each blob's center exactly on its matching dotted ring center (rings encode the blob's color signature; extras are decoys).
- **Key constraint discovered by an early rejected move (L2):** a move is rejected if the blob's whole 5×5 footprint would overlap cyan/wall — so I pixel-mapped terrain each level and pre-verified every intermediate blob position.
- **New mechanic in L5/L6:** white blobs absorb a color sector by landing exactly on a half-colored source (consuming it); combining sectors builds the pattern the ring demands.

**Efficiency:** cost per group = 1 click per star move + 1 click per star switch. I minimized by choosing final star positions that satisfy `sum ∈ [k·target, k·target+k−1]`, ordering waypoints so row/column sums moved monotonically, and chaining consecutive moves of the same star to skip selects (e.g. L6 blob A: 6 moves + 3 selects). Only one action was wasted in the whole run — the rejected move that revealed the terrain rule.
